description: Cryptographic attack based on the birthday paradox, targeting hash functions to find two different inputs that yield the exact same hash (collision).
Forces a system to abandon a secure connection (like TLS 1.3) and fall back to an older, vulnerable protocol version (like SSL 3.0 or TLS 1.0).
Attacker intercepts network traffic (like authentication tokens or encrypted sessions) and retransmits it later to masquerade as an authorized user.
Precomputed table of candidate passwords and their corresponding hashes used to rapidly crack leaked password databases.
Attack against weak hash functions (MD5, SHA-1) where an attacker can append data to the end of a message and calculate a valid hash without knowing the secret key.
Attacker intentionally crafts two distinct files that hash to the exact same value, breaking integrity validation.
